newsitem.title: USA: Forcenergy to increase Alaska oil drilling.
newsitem.headline: Forcenergy to increase Alaska oil drilling.

text.p: Independent oil and gas producer Forcenergy Inc hopes to double its current reserves in the next 18 months through increased drilling in Alaska's Cook Inlet, the company said Thursday.
The Miami-based company plans to drill seven to 10 exploratory wells in the Inlet, which is Alaska's oldest producing area.
"We're trying to find some smaller fields that aren't economical for major (oil companies) but are economic for our size," said Russell Porter, vice president of corporate development for Forcenergy.
The company owns reserves of 108 million barrels of oil equivalent (boe), with 27 million in Alaska and the rest in the U.S. Gulf of Mexico.
If the new wells strike oil, the company could raise its reserves to 260 million boe, Porter said.

Earlier, the company reported second quarter earnings of $3.9 million, $0.16 per share, versus, $1.8 million, or $0.10 a share a year ago. Improved earnings resulted from increased production from its oil and natural gas fields.
